Title: King consents to emergency declaration in Serian
Article:
KUALA LUMOUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the declaration of an emergency throughout the Serian, Sarawak following worsening haze.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of the Prime Minister and the Sarawak Premier, as well as relevant agencies, regarding air quality levels in the affected area.

Title: Teen drowns off Pantai Klebang, mother mourns family's hope
Article:
MELAKA: "He was our hope to care for his sister, who is also a person with disabilities, but he left us first."
Those were the heartbreaking words of Mazan Jaafar, 51, whose 16-year-old son, Muhammad Arif Daniel Nizamuddin, was found drowned after he went swimming with a friend off Pantai Klebang here two days ago.
Mazan, a general assistant at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Rambai, said Arif, the youngest of two siblings, had been the family's hope of caring for his older sister, who has Down syndrome.
She said the siblings shared a close bond, with Arif helping to attend to his sister's needs since he was young.
"Arif was our hope and we had hoped he would care for his sister when we are no longer around.
"He was a good, quiet and obedient boy. If we told him not to do something, he would listen. If we gave him permission, he would do it," she said when met at Melaka Hospital today.
Mazan said caring for his sister had been part of Arif's daily routine, including preparing her breakfast before leaving for college.
Even before the tragedy, Arif had collected nasi lemak from his father at work to bring home for his sister.
Mazan said his sister appeared to realise that her brother was gone, repeatedly calling his name after the incident.
"She kept saying, 'Arif, Arif'. They were very close," she said.
Mazan said Arif would usually inform his parents whenever he planned to go out.
"I did not know he had gone there. As far as I knew, he had gone to school.
"When his friend called my husband to tell us what had happened, we were shocked," she said.
Earlier, media reports said Muhammad Arif was believed to have gone missing while swimming with a friend off Pantai Klebang about 3pm.
His
body was found
by fishermen near Pulau Upeh at 7.20pm, following a two-day search and rescue (SAR) operation.
His remains were buried at the Bukit Rambai Muslim Cemetery.

Title: Court dismisses challenges to 2021 Parliament suspension during Covid-19 emergency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today dismissed legal challenges by two lawmakers, the Malaysian Bar, Bersih 2.0 and several others over the suspension of Parliament during the 2021 Covid-19 emergency.
Judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman ruled that the court could not grant the declarations sought to invalidate provisions of the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance 2021, including Section 14, which dealt with the suspension of Parliament.
She dismissed the two judicial review applications and two originating summons with no order as to costs.
Aliza, however, rejected the government's contention that the proceedings should be dismissed merely because they had become academic following the expiry of the emergency.
The judicial review applications were brought by Pasir Gudang member of parliament Hassan Karim and Perak assemblyman Abdul Aziz Bari.
They had challenged former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's advice to the then Yang di-Pertuan Agong which led to the promulgation of Section 14 of the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance 2021 and the suspension of Parliament.
The Malaysian Bar and Bersih 2.0, together with seven others, had separately filed originating summons challenging aspects of the emergency proclamation and ordinances.

Title: WhatsApp engineers guide Nepal tunnel rescue as two workers found alive
Article:
KATHMANDU: An army of experts in a WhatsApp group is guiding rescue workers scouring a Nepali valley after a huge flash flood more than a week ago as they desperately search for anyone who may be alive inside tunnels of devastated hydropower plants.
The messaging group was set up by engineers before the wall of water, mud and rock crashed down the Trishuli valley in Nepal on Aug 26. It has since become a valuable tool alongside helicopters and heavy machinery in the race to find survivors.
The authorities hope some of the about 900 people reported missing from six hydropower plants - at least three of which were under construction - may have escaped the deluge because they worked in or fled into the tunnels.
In a first sign of success, two people were brought out alive from a tunnel linked to the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday, nine days after the disaster. One of them said there could be more survivors in the tunnels.
Even finding entrances to some of the tunnels, which were designed to channel water or used to access hydropower facilities, is tough now after the flood deposited 2.2 million tonnes of mud and debris down the valley.
'SEND ME LAYOUT DRAWINGS'
"Can you send me Chilime layout drawings," a government official wrote on the engineers' WhatsApp group on Saturday as rescue workers searched the buried remains of the Chilime hydropower plant high in the Himalayan valley close to the Chinese border.
Minutes afterwards, a member of the group chat, which was expanded to add more experts in support of the rescue effort, responded by sending drawings of the project's powerhouse, as well as details of access tunnels.
That exchange and others posted on the group, which has more than 500 members, were seen by Reuters.
Nepal's Independent Power Producers' Association said on Monday at least eight people could be trapped at Chilime, while an official at the Nepal Electricity Authority said 46 may be trapped at Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, further south.
Reuters spoke to a dozen people - including government and military officials, engineers, survivors and relatives of missing workers - who described the efforts to search the tunnel networks of ruined hydropower plants, including how real-time guidance was being provided by experts over WhatsApp.
"The flood has altered the terrain around the tunnels and changed their structure, while mud, rocks, soil and other debris had accumulated inside," Nepal army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet told Reuters. "This is not a normal closure of tunnels."
At Chilime, Reuters images on Monday showed a large tunnel entrance with flood debris rising to the ceiling a short way inside.
More than 1,200 people were killed in last week's deluge caused by a glacier collapse. More than 4,000 people are still missing, including those who might be trapped inside tunnels.
Alongside Chilime, rescue workers are searching five other hydroelectric sites in the valley that were part of an expanding network of plants powering the nation and exporting the surplus. The flood wiped out 10pt of Nepal's generation capacity.
SEEKING ADVICE ABOUT TUNNEL NETWORKS VIA WHATSAPP
At Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, rescue workers reached 250 metres into one tunnel before finding it blocked. But they have not given up the search.
"We are trying to reach there inside again to look for people," said Amshu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal Electricity Authority, adding that 46 people may have been trapped in a chamber, where they might have access to food and water.
A manager at the Nepal Electricity Authority, speaking on condition of anonymity, said rescue workers had also asked former plant employees for advice about the tunnel networks via the WhatsApp group. He said drawings posted on the group had been useful.
At the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower project, rescue workers took almost six days before reaching the tunnel because the entrance was buried, Shahi said. Before the survivors were pulled out on Friday, rescue workers had been trying to supply oxygen via pipes into any cavities in case someone was trapped.
A Reuters photographer who flew to the site on Thursday saw excavators trying to move huge boulders from the mouth of a tunnel and seeking to work their way deeper inside.
Jan Jiwan Thakur, a civil engineer at the Upper Trishuli 1 plant, said a colleague warned him of the coming flood moments before it swept down the valley, giving him enough time to climb to higher ground with about 100 others from the facility.
"We just ran away towards the hillside and, after two to three minutes when we looked down, everything was gone," he said. "The flood debris had entirely covered our office area."
Dhan Bahadur Tamang described escaping through a tunnel when the flood hit, sending pipes and other equipment rushing inside. With knowledge of the tunnel system, he and several others found a way out but he described seeing dead bodies during his subterranean journey to escape.
On the engineers' WhatsApp group, members shared names and mobile phone numbers of missing workers, asking government officials to relay them to telecom authorities in a bid to find their last recorded location.
Meanwhile, family members await news of missing loved ones, like Rajesh Shrestha, whose 30-year-old son, Rajish, is an environmental engineer at Upper Trishuli 1.
"Whenever I look outside, I imagine seeing him carrying a bag and coming home, just as he used to," said Shrestha, who runs a workshop making window grills.
"I am surviving on the hope that he will return."--REUTERS

Title: Nepal floods could cost insurers over US$130 million
Article:
MUMBAI: The devastating flood in Nepal last week could result in commercial insurance losses exceeding 20 billion Nepali rupees (US$132.3 million), with hydropower projects accounting for most claims, according to a top official at one of the country's leading insurers.
The insurance cover, when paid out, covers losses borne by the operators of the power plants.
Life insurance, personal accident and workers' compensation claims are expected separately as authorities verify deaths and missing persons in inaccessible areas.
The disaster on Nepal's border with China's Tibet region caused an estimated US$2.56 billion in economic losses in the Himalayan nation of 30 million people, the country's disaster authority chief told Reuters on Friday, leaving more than 1,200 dead and many more missing.
Eleven Nepali hydropower projects lie in the affected region, some covered by standard commercial insurance policies that are still being assessed, Toton Chakraborty, CEO of Oriental Insurance Company Nepal, told Reuters.
Oriental Insurance Nepal, a unit of the New Delhi-based Indian insurer, is among the leading insurers in the region.
"Hydropower projects along the affected river corridor have suffered the largest damage. In many cases, access roads and above-ground infrastructure have been washed away," he said.
Projects including Rasuwagadhi, Upper Trishuli-3A, Chilime and Devighat, were directly affected, while assessments at five others are ongoing, he said.
Data from the Nepal Insurance Authority show the regulator has so far received 583 flood-related claims worth 25.87 billion Nepalese rupees (US$171.13 million) as of Aug 31.
Chakraborty said these figures largely reflect insured exposure rather than final claims, which will only be clear once detailed surveys are completed.
Claims could rise further if repairs delay project commissioning, as some policies compensate developers for lost revenue resulting from postponed commercial operations, he said.
Nepal's non-life insurance market is small by global standards. The country's 14 non-life insurers generated premiums of about 5.3 billion Nepali rupees (US$35.06 million) during July-August, regulatory data showed, compared with 314 billion Indian rupees (US$3.3 billion) written by Indian insurers during a similar period.
The market is supported by domestic reinsurers Nepal Re and Himalayan Re, alongside international players including India's GIC Re and Germany's Hannover Re.
REINSURERS WARY OF HIMALAYAN RISK
The floods could have lasting implications for insurance coverage of Himalayan infrastructure, four industry executives said.
The Himalayan region faces severe risks from earthquakes and any future glacial floods, a senior UN official told Reuters this week.
"The recent mountain floods in South Asia may lead insurers to further review hydropower and infrastructure risks, particularly in highly exposed locations," said Benjamin Ng, power leader for Asia at Aon, an international insurance broker.
Insurers may increasingly impose exclusions, lower sub-limits and narrow coverage, resulting in higher premiums and more selective underwriting, Ng said.
Other recent Himalayan catastrophes include the 2023 glacial lake outburst flood in India's Sikkim and the flash flood in the northern Indian state of Uttrakhand in 2021.
The latest floods could reshape industry views on risk accumulation and glacial lake outburst flood exposure, said Sanjay Mokashi, chief underwriting officer at Indian state-owned reinsurer GIC Re.--REUTERS

Title: Hadi Awang expected to attend 2026 Umno General Assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang is expected to attend the 2026 Umno General Assembly next week.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who led the Umno delegation to the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar in Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, today said Hadi has confirmed the matter to him.
Asyraf said deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man during the muktamar also expressed his commitment to advancing Muslim unity.
"Insya-Allah, the people are indeed hoping that the two largest Malay and Muslim parties can reach an agreement and work together.
"What is important is the sincerity and trust of both sides, based on the principles and divine guidance," he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Asyraf attended the 72nd Pas Muktamar at the Kelantan Islamic Education Centre (PUTIK), Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, representing Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The presence of Umno's top leadership at the Pas muktamar attracted attention as relations between the country's two largest Malay parties have once again come under the spotlight amid speculation of possible political cooperation between them.
Asyraf said he attended the muktamar on behalf of Zahid, while expressing hope that the understanding between Umno and Pas could continue to be strengthened.

Title: US Navy captain inspired by Sabah community's warmth
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: For US Navy Captain Robert Reyes, it has been a joy to be around the enthusiastic community here.
"As far as the interactions with the children and the community at large, I think everybody has been welcoming and warm, and we could not have asked for better hosts for this project.
"I appreciate their enthusiasm because it gives that excitement to the rest of the engineers as they work on this project," the Pacific Partnership 2026 mission commander told the media after the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the renovation of Babagon Toki Primary School.
[[nid:1525693]]
The Honolulu, Hawaii, native also said he had learned basic expressions including "selamat pagi" and "terima kasih", as well as the Islamic greeting "Assalamualaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh".
"I am a student of language, so I look forward to picking up more," he said.
He said he hoped improvements made at the school under the PP26 community project, including a gazebo and observation deck, would inspire students to realise their potential.
"I think that every young mind has the potential to move mountains, to change the world.
"They just need the opportunity and they need the inspiration."
Reyes said the school project, set against Sabah's scenic surroundings, was intended to provide students with an opportunity to broaden their minds and aspire to greater things.
Over the past 25 days, US Navy Seabees from Naval Mobile Construction Battalion 5 and engineers from the Malaysian armed forces, the Republic of Korea Navy and the Australian army worked side-by-side to renovate the school's infrastructure.
They installed 344 square metres of new non-slip tiles in the outdoor assembly area, made interior electrical improvements, painted the exterior of four school buildings, and constructed a 2-by-2.5m observation deck and gazebo.
"The result you see here is what happens when four countries join in a focused effort to improve the daily lives of students and staff.
"Together, we've strengthened their ability to not only withstand the effects of natural disasters, but we've created an environment that will allow generations to come to not only broaden their horizons but explore their potential."
Reyes said the project, which will benefit 68 students at the school, had been an invaluable learning experience in crossing cultural and linguistic boundaries among personnel from the four nations.
"Speaking to the linguistic challenges, I think those challenges aside, the engineering project is one of a combined effort that shows engineering across nations is almost the same.
"They have their own language, so to speak. What they do not understand or comprehend with their own native languages, they do understand when it comes to the universal language of engineering.
"Because a hammer is a hammer, a nail is a nail, and I think those techniques are pretty much universal."
Pacific Partnership is the US Navy's largest annual multinational humanitarian and civic assistance mission in the Indo-Pacific.
For 20 years, it has brought together militaries, non-governmental organisations and civilian partners from across the region to prepare for crises related to landslides, flooding, earthquakes or tsunamis.
Present were US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires to Malaysia David Gamble and PP26 Exercise Director Colonel Ismail Mohamed.

Title: Anwar: MoF, KKDW should resolve rural road project payment issues amicably
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on the finance ministry (MoF) and rural and regional development ministry (KKDW) to resolve amicably an issue over delayed payments to contractors that had been openly debated between the two ministries.
"Let's discuss this amicably. I want the ministries to discuss it properly, both ministries," he said briefly to the reporters here after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah here today.
Earlier, Zahid has urged the government to
expedite the disbursement of approved allocations
to KKDW to address severe payment delays faced by its contractors.
Zahid who is also KKDW minister said some contractors who had carried out work under KKDW and achieved the progress stipulated under development contracts, including rural road projects, were still facing delays in receiving payments from the government.
The Finance Ministry then refuted claims of budget cuts or restrictions on KKDW allocations for rural road projects, clarifying that all approved funds had been fully channelled.
Treasury secretary-general
Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican
said recent payment delays to contractors stemmed from KKDW having exhausted nearly its entire current-year allocation due to years of overspending beyond its approved parliamentary budgets.
Data released by MoF showed that KKDW had consistently overspent its annual allocation for rural road projects over the past four years.
In 2022, the ministry spent its entire RM1.1 billion allocation. However, expenditure rose significantly in subsequent years, reaching RM1.8 billion against a RM1.1 billion budget in 2023, RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion budget in 2024, and RM2.3 billion against a RM1.6 billion budget in 2025.
For 2026, KKDW had already spent RM1.9 billion of its approved RM2.1 billion allocation as of June.
KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil has then
denied claims
that it overspent its parliamentary allocation, saying payment backlogs stemmed from delayed commitments made during the Covid-19 pandemic, rather than financial mismanagement.
He said portraying the ministry as having spent beyond its allocation gave an inaccurate picture of government financial procedures.

Title: MAG to continue fuel hedging in 2027 as jet fuel costs rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) will continue hedging its fuel costs in 2027 as soaring jet fuel prices put pressure on its finances and prompt the group to trim parts of its network.
MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said the sharp increase in jet fuel prices had put significant pressure on the group's financial performance, prompting a targeted five per cent cut to its network.
"We will continue to monitor demand and market conditions daily to determine the appropriate markets and routes to maintain the group's financial performance," he said at a press conference at the MATTA Fair today.
Fuel accounts for about 40 per cent of MAG's total costs, with every US$1 increase in jet fuel prices translating into an estimated RM50 million increase in annual costs.
MAG, which owns national carrier Malaysia Airlines, is taking a more measured approach to network growth amid the challenging operating environment.
Nasaruddin said the group remained focused on markets where it saw sustainable demand and opportunities to support tourism, trade and connectivity.
"While the operating environment remains challenging, our plans remain firmly focused on the long term," he said.
Despite the cost pressures, Malaysia Airlines has maintained strong operational performance this year.
MAG chief executive officer of airline business Bryan Foong said the airline recorded an average on-time performance (OTP) of 91.11 per cent year to date, exceeding its operational targets and reaching a peak of 93.8 per cent in April.
"To date, we have flown over 10.6 million passengers, with passenger growth of approximately 13 per cent year-on-year.
"Despite the significant growth in passenger demand and volumes, our teams have remained focused on operational reliability, enabling us to maintain and exceed our OTP targets," he said.
Foong said the performance was supported by initiatives including the airline's Fleet Reliability Programme and Schedule Integrity initiatives.
He said MAG's growth was not solely about expanding its network or adding capacity, but also ensuring reliable operations and deploying aircraft and capacity where they could create the most value.
"Growth needs to be supported by strong fundamentals – reliable operations, a consistent customer experience, and making sure we deploy our fleet and capacity where they can create the most value. We are seeing encouraging progress across these areas," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] 35 cloud-seeding operations this year, 90pct yield rain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Some 35 cloud-seeding operations conducted nationwide between Feb 11 and June 21 produced rain in 90 per cent of cases, helping to raise water levels at most targeted dams.
The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) said the operations targeted selected areas and water catchments in Perlis, Kedah, Perak, Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah.
It said the operations were carried out as an early intervention against dry weather, low rainfall and the risk of deteriorating air quality.
"Of the operations carried out, 90 per cent successfully produced rain, helping to raise water levels at most of the targeted dams," the ministry said in a statement.
The operations involved the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), using its Hercules C-130 M30-07 aircraft.
NRES said the government would continue to consider cloud seeding based on need and suitable atmospheric conditions as a mitigation measure against El Nino.
Cloud seeding was also being considered to help address haze, subject to suitable clouds and atmospheric conditions, with operations taking into account the National Haze Action Plan and prevailing air quality.
Meanwhile, a cloud-seeding operation was carried out over northern Peninsular Malaysia yesterday to increase the potential for rainfall and reduce air pollutant concentrations amid dry conditions.
NRES secretary-general Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainudin inspected the operation to observe the process and understand its technical requirements and challenges faced by personnel.
The ministry said her involvement would strengthen coordination between NRES, Nadma, MetMalaysia and RMAF to ensure operations were conducted systematically, efficiently and effectively.
NRES said cloud seeding remained dependent on atmospheric conditions and suitable cloud formation.
It said the initiative reflected the government's preparedness to address dry weather through a data-driven approach, meteorological expertise and continuous monitoring.

Title: Court of Appeal upholds death sentence for deaf, mute man over brutal murder
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A sign language interpreter attracted attention today when she acted as a 'translator' for a deaf and mute man facing the death penalty for murdering a family of four in a fire in Tanjung Sepat, Selangor, nine years ago.
However, the circumstances did not prevent a three-member Court of Appeal panel today from upholding the death sentence against Kang Chang Heng, 47, after unanimously dismissing the former furniture factory worker's appeal to set aside his conviction and sentence.
The panel was led by Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, who sat with Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
In her judgment, Noorin said the Shah Alam High Court was correct in concluding that the prosecution had successfully proven all the essential elements of all the charges beyond reasonable doubt.
"We found no material misdirection, misinterpretation or misunderstanding of the evidence, or error of principle that warranted intervention at the appellate stage.
"Therefore, we uphold the death sentence imposed on the appellant (Kang)," she said.
Kang was found guilty of murdering an elderly couple, Chia Tee Nang, 73, and his wife Lim Mai Shak, 68, who were the parents of his girlfriend, as well as their two grandchildren, Chia Yuan Bin, three, and Ryan Chia, nine.
All four victims died in a fire at a house in Jalan Tepi Laut, Tanjung Sepat, Kuala Langat, between 4am and 5am on Dec 13, 2017.
The Court of Appeal also upheld the nine-year jail sentence against Kang for intentionally causing injury to another grandchild of the couple, Andrew Chia, who was 11 at the time.
Noorin said the court had also considered Kang's defence that he had borrowed money from an illegal moneylender by providing the victims' home address as collateral.
"Kang claimed that he went to the house after being informed that the residence had already been set on fire," she said.
Noorin said that in his defence, Kang himself admitted that he did not tell the 22nd prosecution witness, Christina Chia, that he was at her family home on the morning of the incident, despite knowing that Chia's parents had died in the fire.
"He also admitted that he did not lodge a police report regarding the messages he allegedly received from the illegal moneylender or concerning the burning of the house," she said.
Noorin said the murders were extremely serious and cruel as four victims, including two elderly people and two children, lost their lives in a single incident.
"The evidence accepted by the trial court was that the appellant attacked an elderly woman while she was sitting on a wooden chair, chased her and continued attacking her after she fell.
"The appellant then attacked the first prosecution witness (Andrew), an 11-year-old boy, by slashing his neck twice, in addition to deliberately setting the house on fire," she said.
She said Andrew survived but suffered a violent physical assault after witnessing the incident.
"The court also took into account SP1's evidence that after regaining consciousness, he saw the fire raging and heard the screams of those trapped inside the house," she said.
Commenting on Kang's condition as a deaf and mute person, Noorin said the condition was relevant in considering his personal circumstances and defence.
"However, based on the evidence presented, the condition did not prevent Kang from communicating with others using sign language.
"If Kang had genuinely been there with the intention of saving the victims, the appellant could have sought help from people passing along the road.
"We do not regard the appellant's deaf and mute condition as an aggravating factor, nor do we consider it a sufficiently mitigating factor to outweigh the exceptional seriousness of the offence committed," she said.

Title: No more MACC orange uniform for political leaders in court — Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Political leaders will be given leeway not to wear the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) orange uniform when brought to court, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the leeway had been communicated yesterday, but did not elaborate on whether it was announced at any official meeting or event.
"Yesterday, I also conveyed that before prosecution, when they are brought before the court and charged, they do not need to wear the orange (MACC) uniform.
"If you want to investigate, investigate first. If there is a case to be brought to court, I leave it to the enforcement authorities to decide what colour uniform should be worn.
"For now, I respect the view because there are people who, I think, cooperate with the investigation, so there is no need for them to be made to wear orange, as it would create a different perception," he said after performing Friday prayers and the funeral prayer at Masjid Bukit Indah here today.

Title: Anwar backs tighter oversight of Tabung Haji investments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has backed tighter regulatory oversight of Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) investments, including possible supervision by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).
Anwar said the measure was necessary to prevent abuse of power and other irregularities in TH's management.
The Finance Minister also backed other TH reform initiatives, saying he had been briefed on the proposals.
"This is a measure being taken by the new TH management, led by Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain. I believe this is appropriate and I have already been briefed on the matter, in addition to supporting the implementation of these measures.
"This includes a proposal to amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 so that its management is subject to stricter oversight, either by the SC or BNM, and does not fall through the cracks as happened previously," he said.
The Tambun MP said this at a press conference after attending Friday prayers and performing funeral prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah here today.
Earlier, it was reported that TH planned to place its investment arm under
SC supervision
as part of reforms to its regulatory framework.
TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said the proposal followed extensive discussions by a joint task force involving SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi and BNM governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.
Rashid said the SC was chosen as the primary regulator because between 90 and 95 per cent of TH's total assets were invested in the capital market, rather than held as pure liquidity.
He said the SC's regulatory jurisdiction was therefore aligned with TH's core portfolio, with most of its operations directly linked to capital market investments.
The 211-page Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, which examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020, was completed in July 2022 before being declassified and released to the public last month.
Among its findings, the RCI identified weaknesses in TH's governance and financial management, including accounting practices that resulted in the institution reporting a RM3.4 billion profit in 2017 when it should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion had accounting standards been fully applied.
The commission also highlighted issues involving investment decisions, governance, political interference and the payment of hibah.

Title: Malaysia Airlines returns to Busan after 28 years, Firefly enters China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines Bhd will resume flights to Busan on Dec 2 after a 28-year absence, while sister airline FlyFirefly Sdn Bhd (Firefly) will make its first foray into China with direct services to Kunming.
Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said the new routes reflected the group's focus on markets with sustainable demand and opportunities to support tourism, trade and connectivity.
"These new routes reflect our focus on markets where we see sustainable demand and opportunities to support tourism, trade and people-to-people connections," he said at the MATTA Fair today.
Malaysia Airlines will operate four weekly Kuala Lumpur-Busan flights using Boeing B737-8 aircraft, marking its return to South Korea's second-largest city after last serving the route between 1996 and 1998.
Upon resumption, Malaysia Airlines will be the only carrier offering non-stop flights between Kuala Lumpur and Busan. The service will complement its existing flights to Seoul.
The Busan flights will operate on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays, with introductory return fares starting from RM2,139 for Economy Class and RM4,999 for Business Class.
Meanwhile, Firefly will launch direct flights to Kunming in southwest China using B737-800 aircraft, marking the airline's first route into the country.
"This will open a new connection to an important regional centre, while complementing Malaysia Airlines' network in China, which now serves nine key hubs," Nasaruddin said.
MAG has yet to announce the commencement date or ticket sales for the Kunming service.
Malaysia Airlines will also increase its Kuala Lumpur-Fukuoka services from five times weekly to daily from Dec 1, following the route's resumption on Sept 2.
Brisbane services will increase from six times weekly to daily from Oct 25, with the airline deploying its Airbus A330neo aircraft on the route.
Flights to Surabaya will increase from 14 to 16 times weekly from Nov 1.
Nasaruddin said Malaysia Airlines is also exploring another destination in South Asia, subject to regulatory approvals, with details to be announced in due course.
Separately, MAG is building its own in-flight catering facility near Kuala Lumpur International Airport through MAG Culinary Solutions (MAGCS).
Nasaruddin said groundworks began in July, with the facility targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of 2028 and operations expected to begin in the second quarter of 2029.
The facility is expected to produce about 50,000 meals a day, almost double MAG's current handling capacity, and will cater to the group's airlines and third-party carriers.
MAGCS was established as a MAG subsidiary in September 2025 following the insourcing of Malaysia Airlines' catering operations in 2023.
MAG said customer satisfaction with in-flight dining has increased to 78 per cent from 72 per cent, while catering on-time performance now consistently stands at 99.9 per cent.
The catering unit has secured a Ground Handling Licence and Technical Approval Certificate from the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia, as well as an interim Manufacturing Licence from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority.

Title: NCID strengthens global drug enforcement ties at Argentina conference
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman's Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) is looking to forge closer cooperation with international enforcement agencies, including the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as Malaysia steps up efforts against transnational drug trafficking.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the department was also looking forward to strengthening cooperation with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Drugs, particularly in intelligence sharing and efforts to counter emerging narcotics threats.
This follows Malaysia's participation in the 40th International Drug Enforcement Conference (IDEC XL) 2026 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, which was held from Aug 17 to 21.
Hussein, who led the Malaysian delegation, said the four-day conference provided enforcement agencies with an important platform to exchange experiences and strengthen international networks.
"The conference involved the sharing of global experiences, global networking, discussions on current global trends and specific technical workshops.
"It involved participants from about 160 countries," he told the New Straits Times.
Hussein said the NCID was looking forward to closer cooperation with the DEA and GCC on Drugs following the conference.
The conference, organised by the DEA, brought together law enforcement leaders and senior officers from around the world to strengthen cooperation, intelligence sharing and joint strategies against drug trafficking and transnational organised crime.
"We used the platform to strengthen and coordinate intelligence sharing and international cooperation aimed at preventing synthetic drugs from entering Southeast Asia, including efforts to prevent Malaysia from being exploited as a transit point by drug trafficking syndicates," he said.
Participants represented regions including Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, Europe, Africa, North and Central America, the Southern Cone, the Andean region and the Caribbean.
He said that among the key issues discussed were transnational criminal organisations, synthetic drug markets, cyber investigations and artificial intelligence, changing trafficking routes, port and maritime enforcement, precursor chemicals, and intelligence and information sharing in anti-narcotics operations.
Hussein said Malaysia's participation reflected the police's continued commitment to strengthening strategic international cooperation and intelligence networks to improve efforts against cross-border crime and drug trafficking.
"We can no longer work in silos as doing so would put us at a handicap in dealing with cross-border syndicates.
"Intelligence gathering and sharing information quickly are key to combating the drug trade," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guan Eng calls for action against Zahid over KKDW overspending
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: DAP lawmaker Lim Guan Eng has called for action against Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over alleged overspending by the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW).
The Bagan member of parliament and Air Putih assemblyman said KKDW, under Zahid, should be held accountable for spending beyond approved allocations, warning that such practices could undermine the country's financial stability.
He said the alleged overspending breached existing financial procedures and could warrant enforcement action under relevant laws.
"What Zahid has done directly threatens the country's financial security and economic stability.
"Imagine how serious and harmful the country's financial situation would be if all ministries acted similarly, spending indiscriminately without considering whether the country could afford it," Lim said in a statement on his Facebook page.
Lim said
Finance Ministry (MoF) figures
showed KKDW spending exceeded its approved allocation in each of the past three years.
In 2023, KKDW spent RM1.8 billion against an allocation of RM1.1 billion, while spending in 2024 reached RM2 billion compared with RM1.3 billion allocated.
In 2025, the ministry spent RM2.3 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion.
Lim said the cumulative overspending amounted to RM2.1 billion between 2023 and 2025, during Zahid's tenure at the ministry.
He questioned which contractors benefited from contracts that contributed to the higher expenditure, and whether the contracts were awarded transparently, openly and accountably.
"RM2.1 billion is not a small amount, especially when this was not a problem in the years before 2023," he added.
Lim also drew a comparison with restrictions on support letters issued by ministries other than the MoF, saying such letters could be regarded as concealed government guarantees.
He said only the MoF was authorised under the country's financial laws to issue support letters or guarantees, adding that action had previously been taken over a support letter issued by the Transport Ministry without MoF approval.
Lim said Zahid, as deputy prime minister, should set an example by exercising prudence and restraint in public spending.
He urged Zahid to provide Malaysians with a full explanation over the ministry's spending beyond approved allocations.
Zahid had raised the issue of
delayed payments to contractors
carrying out development projects last Tuesday.
However, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said KKDW had, for several years, made commitments and spent beyond its approved annual allocations for rural road projects.
KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil then denied claims by the MoF that it
overspent its parliamentary allocation
, saying payment backlogs stemmed from delayed commitments made during the Covid-19 pandemic, rather than financial mismanagement.

Title: Kerjaya Prospek's maiden data centre job seen yielding 5-7pct margin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd's (KPG) maiden RM858 million data centre contract is expected to carry a net margin of between five and seven per cent, lower than its usual construction margin as it marks the group's entry into the sector, analysts said.
RHB Research said the RM858 million contract is KPG's largest project win to date, surpassing its previous record of RM710 million for the Astrum Ampang project secured in February 2022.
"Margin-wise, we expect net margins for this job to be between five and seven per cent," it said in a note.
The firm said the latest contract accounts for about 15 per cent of KPG's RM5.9 billion outstanding order book.
"At the same time, we do not discount the possibility of ES Sunlogy Bhd, in which Kerjaya Prospek has a 31 per cent stake, being a potential subcontractor for the data centre job's mechanical and electrical works," it said.
RHB Research said potential involvement in major infrastructure projects, such as the Penang Light Rail Transit, could serve as another catalyst for the construction group.
Kenanga Research expects the project to generate a net margin of between five and six per cent, below KPG's typical 10 per cent level, but viewed the contract positively as a strategic entry into the highly competitive data centre sector.
It said the project's eight-month completion period would support high asset efficiency and optimise working capital deployment.
"This contract elevated year-to-date order replenishment to RM3.23 billion, surpassing our full-year financial year 2026 (FY26) assumption of RM2.5 billion as well as management's RM3.0 billion target.
"This pushed the outstanding order book to RM5.9 billion, providing strong earnings visibility over the next three years," it said.
Kenanga Research raised its FY26 and FY27 job win assumptions to RM3.5 billion and RM2.5 billion, respectively, from RM2.5 billion and RM2.2 billion previously.
It also raised its revenue recognition assumptions to RM2.6 billion and RM3.0 billion from RM2.35 billion and RM2.65 billion, respectively.
"However, we blend down our overall construction net margin assumption slightly to 9.8 per cent (from 10 per cent) to reflect the lower-margin profile of the data centre job.
"All in, our FY26 and FY27 earnings forecasts are upgraded by eight per cent and 10 per cent respectively. Net dividend per share projections remain unchanged at 14.0 sen per annum," it said.
Kenanga Research also raised the target price-to-earnings ratio for KPG's construction business to 18 times from 16 times following its successful entry into the data centre market.

Title: A-GC to appeal ruling allowing Rosmah to adduce fresh evidence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Attorney-General's Chambers will appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor to adduce additional evidence in the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed the move when contacted today.
"We will file the notice of appeal as soon as possible," he told the New Straits Times in a WhatsApp message.
On Sept 1, a three-member Court of Appeal bench allowed Rosmah's application to introduce fresh evidence involving prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, who testified as the 16th prosecution witness during the trial.
The bench, chaired by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, ruled that
Rosmah
had established a prima facie case for the admission of the additional evidence.
The other judges were Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy.
Choo, who delivered the ruling, said the appellate court was not required at that stage to determine whether Rayyan's latest account was true, as his credibility could be tested through cross-examination.
The additional evidence includes allegations that Rayyan had been subjected to prosecutorial pressure during the trial, a statutory declaration and newly recovered WhatsApp communications.
It also concerns allegations over the suppression of Rayyan's statement recorded under Section 112 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
The court held that the fresh evidence, if accepted as true, could materially affect the factual findings made by the trial judge and potentially alter the evidential basis of Rosmah's conviction.
It ordered the additional evidence to be taken before a different High Court judge within two weeks.
Rayyan is to be recalled to testify and will be subjected to cross-examination and re-examination.
Rosmah is appealing against her conviction and sentence over the solar hybrid project involving 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
On Sept 1, 2022, the High Court found her guilty of three corruption charges and sentenced her to 10 years' jail and fined her RM970 million.
She was convicted of soliciting RM187.5 million from former Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin, through her former aide Rizal Mansor, as an inducement to help the company secure the project.
Rosmah was also found guilty of receiving RM5 million from Saidi through Rizal at Seri Perdana in Putrajaya on Dec 20, 2016, and another RM1.5 million at Jalan Langgak Duta on Sept 7, 2017.
Her jail sentence and fine have been stayed pending the disposal of her appeal.

Title: Harmonised standards, 'single window' clearance key to seamless JS-SEZ cross-border trade
Article:
SINGAPORE: Establishing a single-window trade system and harmonising regulatory standards between Malaysia and Singapore are vital steps to achieve seamless cross-border integration and fully unlock the economic potential of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), according to a leading express logistics company.
While physical connectivity across the Causeway remains robust, non-tariff regulatory processes continue to present operational friction for cross-border cargo movements between both nations.
FedEx Malaysia managing director Woon Tien Long highlighted that despite strong bilateral trade ties, compliance with distinct national regulatory frameworks requires streamlined coordination.
"We are still two sovereign countries governed by our own specific laws; when you talk about ISO standards, they are universally recognised, but in a clearance or regulatory environment, recognising another country's licensing and certifications would help smooth trade.
"A single window of trade would be able to unlock this seamlessness, eliminating the need to apply for double import permits," he told a recent interview session during the FedEx Johor-Singapore Cross-Border Media Tour at FedEx South Pacific Regional Hub Singapore.
Speaking on supply chain readiness ahead of the expected rollout of the JS-SEZ Master Plan this December, Woon emphasised that managing logistics across the corridor requires continuous adaptation as trade volumes expand.
"There is no hard and fast rule because every customer, depending on the industry you are in, will have different needs; our job as an integrator is then to find ways to fulfil that need for you," he said.
Logistics operators are also advocating for the digital and physical replication of automated border clearances for goods, similar to recent passenger travel enhancements and drive-through X-ray inspection tunnels. ​
"Human movement improvements like QR code scanning came first because passenger queues generate immediate feedback, but now we are advocating for cargo needs so trade flows just as smoothly," Woon noted.
Echoing these views, FedEx Singapore managing director Eric Tan revealed that the logistics industry has actively lobbied both governments to address redundant border procedures.
"Imagine if you are a customer or a service provider—you want to eliminate double handling and duplication as much as possible, and ideally, all paperwork and checks should only be performed once," he emphasised.
Tan highlighted that in October 2025, FedEx published a joint white paper in conjunction with the Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) to serve as a strategic roadmap for an innovation-led, resilient cross-border ecosystem.
"While it is still a work in progress, this push for seamless trade benefits the entire industry, including competitors and end-consumers," he stated.
To support this economic growth, FedEx has already optimised its network routing to send inbound shipments from Asia, Europe, and the United States directly from its Singapore gateway to Senai customs.
This network adjustment bypasses a previous 300-kilometre detour through Kuala Lumpur, accelerating delivery transit times into Johor by up to two hours.
Tan noted that bilateral trade between Malaysia and Singapore reached RM402.35 billion (US$93.97 billion) in 2025, up 1.5 per cent from 2024, with both countries remaining each other's second-largest trading partners.

Title: Almost 99pc Malaysia Airlines cabin crew drug tested, all negative
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: About 98.8 per cent of Malaysia Airlines cabin crew have undergone drug screening, with all tests returning negative, said Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG).
MAG managing director and chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said drug screening would be made a mandatory annual requirement for all cabin crew.
He said safety remained a non-negotiable priority for the group as it continued to strengthen its safety processes and standards.
Nasaruddin said MAG had also completed drug screening for more than 1,500 pilots across its airlines, including all pilots and cabin crew of Firefly, on Aug 15.
"As of yesterday, about 98.8 per cent of Malaysia Airlines cabin crew (had undergone screening), and we hope to reach 100 per cent today," he said at a press conference here today.
To date, all tests involving Malaysia Airlines and Firefly crew have returned negative results.
"We also conduct random testing almost every week.
"Safety requires discipline in every decision we make, the standards we set and how we respond when something does not go as planned," he said.
He said focusing on operational fundamentals was increasingly important as the aviation industry faced various external pressures, including fuel price fluctuations, supply chain constraints and geopolitical uncertainty.
Although demand remained encouraging, the group continued to face challenges from fuel prices, market volatility, supply chain constraints and geopolitical uncertainty.
"Fuel alone accounts for almost 40 per cent of MAG's total operating costs. Every US$1 increase in fuel prices has an impact of about RM50 million on our costs," he said.
Nasaruddin said while the group might not be able to control these external pressures, it could determine its level of preparedness and response to such challenges.
This included strengthening its business operations and safety measures to enhance competitiveness, as well as offering products and experiences that meet and are valued by customers, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Economy Ministry examines Malaysia's preparedness for an ageing nation in 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry is examining the structure of the country's preparedness as Malaysia moves towards becoming an ageing nation, through Budget 2027.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said this is important to ensure the sustainability and continuity of the country's economic growth, as well as to empower the next generation.
"The younger generation needs to shoulder greater responsibility for the sustainability of the economy and the continuity of the country's growth (as we transition to an ageing nation).
"Therefore, to delve into this issue, the Economy Ministry is examining the structure of the country's preparedness for an ageing population, not only focusing on managing an elderly population, but also on preparing the younger generation for their future well-being," he said after officiating the Junior Innovathon: Di Sini Inovasi Bermula here today.
In youth development context, Akmal Nasrullah said his ministry aims to broaden their exposure to specialised programmes and to identify, in particular, economic structures and opportunities that remain unclear to them.
"We want to create opportunities for young people to explore one or two segments previously not open to them, particularly in terms of the stock market and ownership.
"This will enable them to learn about and venture into another segment or new sector," he said.
Akmal Nasrullah also said education in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) need to be strengthened through talent development from the grassroots level.
"We are giving priority to enabling these talents by equipping them with the necessary skills to become more directly involved in high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries.
"At the same time, we are strengthening funding for research and invention, not only for academic purposes, but also for commercialisation," he added.
Junior Innovathon Season Two 2026, a television programme produced by Radio Televisyen Malaysia, will begin airing on Sept 20. It features the top 50 teams selected from 2,092 entries and culminates in selecting the champion on Nov 1, 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two trapped tunnel workers rescued in Nepal 'miracle'
Article:
KATHMANDU, (Nepal): Two hydropower workers were pulled alive from a tunnel buried by debris in Nepal on Friday, a rare ray of hope on the tenth day of rescue efforts after catastrophic Himalayan flooding.
Rescuers cheered as one man was pulled through a muddy opening, a video released by the energy ministry showed.
He was helped to his feet by rescuers, and later carried on the backs of the emergency workers, raising his hand as they took him towards a helicopter.
A photograph showed the second man caked in mud, his hands pressed together in prayer, as rescuers carried him on a stretcher.
"As long as there is breath, there is hope!" Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said in a statement.
"Rescue operations are continuing in all the affected tunnels. Let everyone's efforts and prayers continue. We have not lost hope."
Rescuers called it a "miracle" after the August 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border, that has killed at least 1,280 people and left more than 5,500 missing.
"I am so happy, my heart is lighter," Amir Maharjan, the brother of rescued worker Kabir Maharjan, told AFP.
The men, both Nepali, were named as Sanjay Shah, 30, a mechanical foreman, as well as Maharjan, 45, a mechanical supervisor, by Home Minister Sudan Gurung.
The prime minister's office said that Shah was in a "stable condition", and that Maharjan was in intensive care.
- '24/7 heartache' -
Lakshmi Naini, who said Maharjan is her brother-in-law, waited outside a hospital in Kathmandu, where he was rushed to by helicopter.
"It's a miracle! I am very happy," she told AFP. "I heard he is alive through social media, and I could not believe it."
"I have no words to express how I feel," said another relative, Shyam Maharjan, 45.
The two were among hundreds of hydropower workers who had been missing since a wall of mud and debris swept through the region on August 26 after a vast glacial and rock collapse on a mountain on the China-Nepal border.
Searches were continuing at the Trishuli 3A tunnel where the two men were rescued, as well as multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects smashed by the floods.
The government had initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.
Nepali rescuers, aided by experts from India, China and South Korea, have continued searching for survivors feared trapped inside hydropower tunnels, but teams had repeatedly hit walls of hard-packed debris.
Until Friday, none of the tunnel workers had been confirmed alive.
Australian rescue expert Arnold Dix, who has been supporting the operation remotely, told AFP that the rescue efforts were "back in miracle country" after a "week of 24/7 heartache."
Earlier Friday, Dix said teams at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project believed they had heard a faint response from inside the tunnel.
"They believe they received a faint response from inside saying, 'hunchha', yes or OK," Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, told AFP, adding that he was en route to Nepal to join the rescue effort.
He said rescuers had called into the tunnel: "Don't worry, we are rescuing you."
Dix was a key adviser during the Himalayan rescue effort that successfully freed all 41 Indian workers trapped inside a collapsed under-construction road tunnel in 2023.
Dix said teams had dug through debris blocking the tunnel for 50 to 60 metres (164-196 feet) and had been hoping for a breakthrough at any moment.
Less than an hour later, rescuers pulled the two men to safety.
- 'Himalayan tsunami' -
Some Nepali families who were searching for their missing loved ones had begun holding symbolic funerals in the last few days, in a sign of dimming hope for survivors.
Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has called the gigantic wave triggered by a rock and ice avalanche a "Himalayan tsunami."
Floods had tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and multiple hydropower dams that day.
AFP reporters flying by helicopter over the valley of destruction on Thursday saw entire sections of settlements swept away, leaving the landscape resembling a puzzle with pieces missing.
Picturesque villages of green paddy fields and houses sat beside vast chunks of land washed away.
Communities near the epicentre remain cut off.
The United Nations has warned that the "magnitude of the destruction" makes delivering aid an immense challenge, with cargo drones and porters being considered to reach isolated communities.
"Access has been very, very, very difficult," UN chief in Nepal Lila Pieters Yahia said.
Nepal's disaster authority says number of bodies recovered is 1,259, with 5,083 people missing. In China, state media say 21 people had been killed, and 541 people are missing.
That takes the overall toll to 1,280 people, with 5,624 missing.
More than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries are among those missing, including tourists and pilgrims, in both Nepal and Tibet in China. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar open to consider early general election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is open to considering calls for an early general election.
Anwar, however, said any decision would be made after careful consideration before being presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
He was responding to calls by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for an early election.
"That is a proposal I can consider, but the decision will be made by me after I have thought about it. I will then present it to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah, Ampang, here.
However, Anwar said the government's immediate focus remained on the economy, the welfare of the people and efforts to rid the country of corruption and abuse of power.
"For me, these are the important focuses. Given the current situation, the government remains stable, and we should concentrate on these matters," he said.
Anwar added that those entrusted with public responsibilities and who had clean records should not fear investigations by enforcement agencies, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), police and Inland Revenue Board.
He said the government had a mandate to administer the country properly and tackle corruption and abuse of power regardless of political or racial considerations.
"We cannot continue to allow the current situation to persist.
"We have been given the mandate to govern and manage the country well and to clean it of corruption and abuse of power," he said.
Anwar also stressed that enforcement agencies must carry out investigations fairly and based on evidence.
"If there is evidence, proceed. If there is no evidence, release them," he said.
He said he had also conveyed his position to the cabinet that enforcement agencies must carry out their duties professionally and fairly, rejecting allegations that investigations were being used to target particular individuals.
Anwar said he was prepared to face pressure in pursuing the government's anti-corruption agenda, stressing that the effort was not aimed at protecting his position or any particular group.
"This is not about race. This is about saving the country.
"It is not about saving a position or saving a group," he said.
He said he hoped the public would continue to support efforts to strengthen governance and clean up the country.
Previously, Zahid who is Umno president has voiced support for an earlier 16th General Election (GE16) saying this would allow the government to seek a
fresh mandate
from the people.
The Barisan Nasional chairman said the coalition was nevertheless prepared to face the polls if the current parliament served its full term.
Hadi meanwhile said
Pas is ready for the GE16
, whether it is held earlier than scheduled or otherwise.
He said the party was prepared for the election, including having its candidates ready.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citi eyes China brokerage unit licence as soon as this month
Article:
HONG KONG: Citigroup expects to get regulatory approval for its wholly-owned China brokerage business as soon as this month and plans to add several dozen staff at the unit over the next few months, said two people with knowledge of the matter.
The long-awaited final Chinese regulatory approval for the business could be granted around the time of Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned visit to Washington to meet with US President Donald Trump in late September, the sources said.
The expected regulatory approval for the business as soon as this month has not been reported previously.
Citi declined to comment.
The US bank, which offers corporate, institutional and other banking services in China, applied for a wholly-owned mainland Chinese brokerage unit licence in late 2021 as part of its push to ramp up its presence in the world's second-largest economy.
Citi, which has been hiring for the business over the last couple of years in preparation for the licence, aims to roughly double the headcount to around 100 people by the end of this year, said the first source.
The China expansion would see Citi competing with already licensed Wall Street rivals including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley for a share of growing and increasingly profitable onshore securities trading and underwriting deals.
The expected launch of Citi's brokerage business comes at a time when China is seeing a growing list of technology and other companies tapping domestic equity markets for fundraising and attracting increased fund flows into the stock markets.
Despite intense Sino-US geopolitical tensions in recent years, Beijing has been expanding Wall Street firms' access to its financial sector worth trillions of dollars as it looks to attract more capital inflows.
The New York-headquartered bank's China hiring push will see it adding people from senior front-office bankers to support staff and will be done via a combination of internal transfers and external hires, the sources said.
They declined to be named as the expansion plans are not public.
For the China brokerage unit, Citi plans to relocate some of its bankers from Hong Kong and other markets in Asia, as well as moving some of its existing mainland staff to the new business, the first source added.
COMPETITIVE MARKET
In 2025, profits at the wholly-owned China securities unit of Goldman Sachs nearly tripled to 1.46 billion yuan ($217.39 million), while JPMorgan's almost quadrupled to 984 million yuan, as per their latest China annual reports.
Morgan Stanley's profit soared sevenfold to 138 million yuan last year, its annual report showed, as the US banks benefit from surging securities trading revenue primarily from institutional clients.
Citi's new China business unit is seeking a regulatory nod to conduct A-share brokerage, underwriting, research and principal trading businesses in the onshore market, according to the sources.
Those offerings would complement the bank's existing offshore-focused China investment banking team that supports domestic companies' financing activities in overseas markets, the first source added.
The bank plans to lean on its sizeable onshore corporate and commercial banking client base, which it already serves in areas such as foreign exchange, cash management and trade finance, to win A-share equity and M&A mandates, the people said.
For the new unit, Citi will focus on sectors including technology, healthcare, consumer and financial institutions, targeting China's established corporate "champions" as well as emerging players including AI and chip companies.
Citi this week announced a 25 per cent headcount increase across South Africa, Europe and Asia to serve its North Asian clients' outbound banking needs, including those from mainland China.
In addition to the Wall Street rivals, Citi would be competing with the dominant Chinese brokerages for its planned offering. Some foreign financial firms have exited the country in the recent past due to the hyper-competitive business environment.
Reuters reported last month that asset manager Fidelity International was planning to wind down a China fund management unit, which followed Schroders' decision to transfer its onshore team and products to peer Neuberger Berman.
The planned China expansion comes against the backdrop of Citi CEO Jane Fraser, who was the sole female global banking chief accompanying Trump on his May visit to Beijing, pushing for stronger profitability targets for the next two years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN yet to decide Bersatu's position in coalition, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has yet to decide on Bersatu's position in the coalition following Pas' decision to end its political cooperation with the party.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the matter would be discussed at a special meeting, although no date had been set.
He said the coalition was still making the necessary arrangements for the meeting.
"At the moment, we are busy with the muktamar. So, the decision to hold the meeting is expected to be made next week.
"After the meeting, we will call them to seek an explanation," the Pas deputy president said when met at 72nd Pas Muktamar here today.
Tuan Ibrahim said so far Bersatu remained a member of PN.
The status of Bersatu in PN has come under scrutiny following Pas' decision to end its political cooperation with the party.
On Aug 28, Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said
the rift between Pas and Bersatu
has widened further after Pas declared that the door to reconciliation between the two parties is now closed.
He said this stance follows Bersatu's decision to contest against PN in the Negri Sembilan state election on Aug 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore's tax revenue up 9.4pct to S$97.3bil
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore collected S$97.3 billion (S$1=RM3.19) in tax revenue for financial year (FY) 2025/2026, up by 9.4 per cent compared with the preceding year amid stronger economic activity and consumer spending, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) said.
In a statement today, IRAS said the total tax revenue collected accounts for 74.8 per cent of the Singapore Government's operating revenue and 12.3 per cent of Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP).
"Beyond tax collection, IRAS processed close to S$1.2 billion in payouts to support businesses and workers, contributing to national resilience and inclusive growth.
"The arrears rate for income tax, Goods and Services Tax (GST), and property tax remains low at 0.64 per cent of net tax assessed," the statement said.
According to IRAS, corporate income tax increased to S$34.4 billion in FY25, up from S$30.9 billion in FY24. It remained the largest source of IRAS' revenue collection, accounting for 35.4 per cent of the total.
GST was the second-largest contributor at 22.3 per cent (S$21.7 billion), up from S$20.0 billion in FY24, reflecting higher consumer spending.
Income tax for individuals accounted for the third-largest share of IRAS' revenue collection at 21.5 per cent (S$20.9 billion), up from S$19.1 billion in FY24.
This was followed by property tax and stamp duty, which contributed 7.1 per cent (S$6.9 billion) and 7.5 per cent (S$7.3 billion) of IRAS' revenue collection, respectively.
"Taxpayers continue to demonstrate strong compliance across all tax types, reinforcing IRAS' role in shaping a responsible taxpaying community.
The statement said the IRAS supports timely and accurate compliance and has made tax filing and payment simple and accessible through sustained public outreach.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver arrested over crash that killed 12-year-old motorcyclist
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: Police have arrested a lorry driver involved in an accident that killed a 12-year-old boy who was riding a motorcycle along Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday.
The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, died at the scene from severe injuries.
Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the 40-year-old man was detained to assist with investigations.
"The suspect has been remanded for three days from today to assist investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving," he said when contacted.
The offence carries a jail term of five to 10 years, a fine of between RM20,000 and RM50,000, and disqualification from holding a driving licence for up to five years.
In yesterday's crash, the boy was riding a motorcycle when he collided with the rear left side of the lorry.
His 14-year-old pillion rider escaped with minor scratches and cuts on his hands and legs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Putrajaya, Sarawak in talks over Serian haze as API breaches 500
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The federal government is in discussions with the Sarawak government over the worsening haze in Serian, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) has breached 500.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had been in contact with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, with both sides discussing further measures to address the situation.
"We are in contact with the state government and the Premier of Sarawak. We have been in discussions for the past two days," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah, Ampang, today.
Asked when an emergency would be declared, Anwar said the matter was still under discussion.
"We are discussing it. I will know more after this," he said.
He added that authorities were preparing to take all necessary measures to protect residents, including the possible closure of schools and offices, while essential security agencies would continue operating.
Anwar said the government would also consider cloud seeding and other measures to alleviate the haze.
"We will take all the necessary measures, including cloud seeding and whatever else is needed," he said.
He said the haze was partly linked to developments in other areas, with Sarawak among the states affected.
He urged residents to remain patient while authorities worked to address the situation.
"I pray for the safety of the people of Serian, Sarawak and others who have been affected," he said.
As of 2pm today, Serian remained at hazardous levels, with the API
reaching 521
.
A check of the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website showed Kuching was the only other location to record a hazardous reading, at 311.
Two locations recorded very unhealthy readings – Samarahan (284) and Sri Aman (235).
Meanwhile, 11 locations recorded unhealthy readings: Sarikei (182), Sibu (181), Mukah (177), Bintulu (157), Kota Kinabalu (152), Tawau (151), Samalaju (146), Sandakan (140), Pasir Gudang, Johor (128), Segamat, Johor (115), and Miri (112).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.
Readings above 500 indicate extremely severe pollution and may prompt immediate emergency action by the authorities, depending on the circumstances.

Title: 'Sayang, you ok?': Malaysian's last words to wife before fatal stabbing in South Korea
Article:
RAWANG: The widow of a Malaysian who was stabbed to death while trying to break up a fight in South Korea in July said her husband managed to check on her in his dying moments.
Nurcahaya Ruslan, 34, said her husband, Ahmad Shah Ahmad Ros, 26, was bleeding heavily from his stab wound, but still made his way to her.
"He asked, 'Sayang, you ok?', even though he had been stabbed and blood was gushing out," Nurcahaya said when contacted.
"On the night of the incident, my husband and I had burgers and watched a movie together."
She said her husband then received a call from a friend who needed help. They went out to help the friend, who was involved in a fight.
"My husband went to break up the fight when he was stabbed. I screamed in shock when I saw it.
"He still came over to check on me despite his injuries. I was angry and asked the group who they were and why they did that to my husband.
"Other friends then rushed him to the hospital. On the way, he was still alive and asked for water," she said.
Nurcahaya said Ahmad Shah died while receiving treatment at the hospital.
"I accept his passing, but I remain sad and traumatised as it happened right before my eyes, especially when night comes," said Nurcahaya, who worked at the same factory as her husband in South Korea.
A Malaysian man in his 40s was arrested by South Korean police after the fatal stabbing.
She quit her job and returned to Malaysia on Aug 28, but continues to monitor the murder case with the help of friends in South Korea.
She said court proceedings were underway, but the suspect had not been sentenced, adding that she hoped the perpetrator would receive an appropriate punishment.
"Authorities and friends advised me to stay in South Korea until the case was resolved, as it was not expected to take long.
"However, I was not strong enough to stay there. I kept remembering my husband and cried almost every day as our home was full of memories, so I returned to Malaysia after settling several matters.
"Now, friends there are following the court case with the help of a Korean friend fluent in Malay, who translates the proceedings for us," she said.
