Title: Anwar tells Rural Development Ministry and MOF to find middle ground in funding row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to resolve issues concerning allocations, including delayed payments to contractors, through discussions.
“Let us discuss this amicably. I have asked both ministries to resolve this properly,” he said briefly when asked to comment on the matter.
He was speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah, Ampang Jaya, here today.
On Thursday, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said there were no restrictions on KKDW allocations for rural road projects, with the full allocation for the projects having already been channelled.
He said constraints in the payment process to contractors were due to the current year’s allocation having been almost fully utilised.
The issue arose following a statement by Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi regarding problems faced by contractors following delays in payments for projects under his ministry. — Bernama

Title: Anwar endorses proposal for SC or BNM oversight of Tabung Haji investments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today backed a proposal by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to place its investment operations under the regulatory oversight of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said the move was appropriate to ensure TH’s operations were subject to tighter regulation and to prevent abuse of power and other governance-related issues in the future.
He said the initiative by TH’s new management, led by its chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, was a positive step towards strengthening governance and accountability at the pilgrimage fund management institution.
“This is, in my view, appropriate, and I have been briefed by them and support the measures, including several proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Bukit Indah, Ampang Jaya, here today.
He added that the move would ensure tighter oversight of TH’s management by either the SC or BNM and prevent governance weaknesses from going unchecked, as had happened previously.
Yesterday, Abdul Rashid said TH was refining a new regulatory framework to place its investment operations under the statutory oversight of the SC.
He said the decision followed nearly six months of detailed deliberations by a joint task force, which was established to examine the proposed regulatory framework.
The task force also comprises the SC chairman and BNM Governor, with the aim of ensuring TH’s investment management complies with Malaysia’s capital market regulatory standards. — Bernama

Title: Eight men charged with murder over fatal Taman Alam Megah brawl
Article:
SHAH ALAM,  Sept 4 — Eight men, including two alleged secret society members, were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a man during a brawl involving a group of individuals in Taman Alam Megah last month.
Soulami Ahimsha, 46; S.R. Harikrisnan, 42; M.K. Puwaneswaran, 39; A. Rhubban, 37; K. Thivagar, 29; Shaik Hasanudin Ahlauwudin, 26; Sheikh Mauludin Ahlauwudin, 24; and R. Darvin Raj, 23, nodded after the charge was read out to them before Magistrate Cynthia Noor Haizean Sulaiman.
No plea was recorded from any of the accused as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, they, together with eight others still at large, as members of an unlawful assembly with a common intention, are accused of murdering Ganesan, 23, at Jalan Mandolin, Taman Alam Megah here at 1.59pm on August 25.
They were charged under Section 149 of the Penal Code and are liable to punishment under Section 302 of the same code; a conviction carries the death penalty or imprisonment for a term of 30 to 40 years, and if not sentenced to death, the offender shall also be liable to whipping of not less than 12 strokes.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Alya Zaphfirah Al Zaphni, while lawyers Navin Punj and Nur Aida Md Zainuddin represented three of the accused. The remaining accused were unrepresented.
The court denied bail and fixed October 13 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Prosecution to appeal Rosmah ruling allowing additional evidence, says AG
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The prosecution will appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence for corruption involving the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed that the prosecution would file the appeal.
“It merits an appeal to the Federal Court. We will file it as soon as possible,” he said.
Under the law, a notice of appeal must be filed within 14 days of the court’s decision.
On Tuesday, a three-man bench of the Court of Appeal comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to submit additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction and sentence.
The court ordered that the additional evidence be obtained from prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah through further cross-examination and re-examination. It also ordered that any other evidence to be introduced by either the defence or prosecution must be related to Rayyan’s additional evidence.
The Court of Appeal further ordered that the additional evidence be recorded before a new High Court judge within two weeks of the case management, which is scheduled for September 10.
Rosmah, the wife of former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, had sought to adduce additional evidence comprising a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by Rayyan, who had alleged that he was subjected to prosecutorial pressure during the trial.
On September 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and accepting RM6.5 million in bribes from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The bribes were an inducement for Rosmah to assist Jepak Holdings in securing the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project for 369 rural schools in Sarawak from the Education Ministry.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending her appeal.
The Court of Appeal has fixed October 4 to16 and October 19 to 23 for the hearing of her appeal. — Bernama

Title: Court rules DNAA not applicable in Maju Holdings director, wife’s CBT, money laundering case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Sessions Court here has rejected an application for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering case involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife.
The Star
reported that the application was made by Abu Sahid’s lawyer, Datuk Jasbeer Singh, who argued that the prosecution had yet to hand over several key documents despite the case having been mentioned seven times since the accused was charged last year.
“It has been one year since my client was charged and there have been seven case mention proceedings for the prosecution to submit documents,” he told the court.
“The volume of documents is not important — what matters now is whether the evidential issue has been covered under Section 51A of the Criminal Procedure Code pertaining to delivery of documents,” he said.
Jasbeer argued that the charge should not have been brought while investigations were still incomplete.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nidzuwan Abd Latif said the prosecution would provide five more volumes of documents, although some material was still pending.
He said the delay was due to the prosecution having to liaise with relevant authorities and agencies, adding that outstanding documents could still be supplied before trial to give the defence sufficient time to prepare.
Nidzuwan also told the court that the prosecution was ready for the High Court to fix a trial date.
Judge Suzana Hussin dismissed the DNAA application, ruling that such an order was not relevant in the case.
The court directed that the next mention be used to fix a trial date and instructed the prosecution to prepare a list of witnesses and submit any remaining documents required by then.
The next mention was fixed for November 20.
Abu Sahid claimed trial to 17 charges involving CBT and money laundering linked to the proposed MEX II Highway project on September 8 last year.
He faces four CBT charges involving RM313 million and 13 money laundering charges involving RM139 million, allegedly committed between May 2016 and October 2019.
The CBT charges are under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries up to 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping and a possible fine upon conviction.
The money laundering charges were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, which carries up to 15 years’ imprisonment and a fine of at least five times the proceeds from unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
MEX II is a proposed 18km highway linking Putrajaya to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), with construction beginning in 2016 before the project was halted over financial problems.
Abu Sahid also faces seven additional charges of misusing property under Section 403 of the Penal Code involving RM145 million.
His wife, Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi, was separately charged on Sept 8 last year with receiving RM67.14 million in proceeds allegedly linked to unlawful activities into her bank account from an account belonging to Abu Sahid between March and November 2017.
She was charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the same Act and claimed trial.

Title: BN backs unity govt despite push for earlier GE16, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Barisan Nasional remains committed to the unity government and the country’s political stability despite calls within the coalition for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held earlier, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir.
The Star
reported that Zambry said BN’s support for the unity government remained firm, stressing that calls for an earlier election should not be interpreted as confidence that the coalition would automatically regain federal power.
“Although Umno and Barisan may want an earlier election, it does not mean we are overconfident that we will win and form the government,” he said.
“Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has also stressed many times that this country needs to remain stable and he has made a clear commitment,” he added.
Zambry said this after launching the Asia Pacific University (APU) Artificial Intelligence (AI) Supercomputing Lab powered by NVIDIA DGX Sparks here today.
He said there was no intention among BN’s partners to undermine or bring down the unity government before the next general election.
“The question of poking holes in the roof (tebuk atap) does not arise at all because we are committed to maintaining this government until the election date is announced,” he said.
Zambry added that this remained BN’s position as a partner in the Madani government.
His comments followed Zahid’s recent support for GE16 to be held earlier, with the BN chairman saying a sooner election would allow the government to seek a fresh mandate from voters.
Zahid had also said BN was prepared to contest GE16 at the end of the current parliamentary term if it ran its full course.
The 15th Parliament is expected to complete its full term on December 18, 2027.

Title: Malaysian man jailed six years in Australia for keeping Indonesian woman as slave
Article:
MELBOURNE, Sept 4 — A Malaysian man has been sentenced to six years in prison in Australia after being convicted of enslaving and assaulting an Indonesian woman.
Free Malaysia Today, citing ABC News, reported that Melbourne County Court Judge Michael Cahill sentenced Chong Chee Kit, 47, after a jury found him guilty of forcing the woman into domestic servitude and subjecting her to repeated abuse.
“You treated her as a slave, that is, you used her like property you owned,” Cahill said, describing Chong’s conduct as callous and cruel.
The judge said Chong subjected the woman to physical abuse over minor mistakes, including kicking her in the face and smashing her head against a wall.
The court heard that Chong restricted her access to food and medical treatment, controlled where she went and prevented her from getting adequate sleep.
Chong will be eligible for parole in 2030 and is expected to be deported to Malaysia after serving his sentence.
A jury in May found Chong guilty of keeping the woman, who was in her 60s, in slavery between February and October 2022.
His wife, Angie Liaw, was acquitted of charges that she had helped or encouraged Chong to keep the woman in slavery.
The couple had been charged together in 2023.
The court heard Chong met the woman at a church in Malaysia in 2015 and developed what was described as a “mother-son” relationship with her.
She moved to Australia in 2017 to live with the couple, but they later returned to Malaysia without informing her, leaving her without accommodation for four years.
In 2021, they told her they had returned to Melbourne and offered to employ her for a month.
She moved into their home in early 2022 after Liaw gave birth to her second child, initially planning to stay for only a month.
The court heard Chong also made the woman borrow money from relatives to cover house rent and hospital expenses related to the birth.
She escaped from the home in October 2022 and was missing for several days before police found her and took her to hospital, where the circumstances surrounding her treatment came to light.
Slavery is a federal offence in Australia punishable by up to 25 years in prison.
The woman died of natural causes in 2024.

Title: Penang steps up action to curb sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 4 — The Penang state government has taken several measures to address sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat, near Tasek Gelugor, including requiring all farms in the area to send their wastewater to a biogas plant in Ampang Jajar.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the move is part of the state government’s efforts to prevent livestock farm sewage from being discharged directly into drains or rivers in the area.
“The matter was discussed at a meeting with the state Veterinary Services Department and the state assemblyman for the area in April, and the state government has required all pig farms in Kampung Selamat to send their sewage waste to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar since May.
“The Veterinary Services Department conducts weekly monitoring, while officers will investigate any complaints received. Surprise inspections are also carried out in the absence of complaints, but so far, no farms in the area have been found discharging sewage directly into drains or rivers,” he told reporters after the opening ceremony of SkyGate NHJ Technology Sdn Bhd in Perai today.
He said this when asked to comment on media reports about Tasek Gelugor MP Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan’s call for the government and authorities to take immediate action to address sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat, which he claimed had burdened residents for decades.
Wan Saiful was reported to have said that he and the Tasek Gelugor Action Committee were seeking to gather scientific evidence of the pollution, including through sampling in the Parit Cina area.
H’ng said the state government is also considering the issue of sediment and old sewage waste that had accumulated in the area’s drains over the years.
“Once the clean-up of the old waste is completed, the state government plans to allocate funding for the Drainage and Irrigation Department to carry out desilting work on the drains,” he said.
He said the state would adopt a similar approach to that taken in Kampung Valdor, Sungai Bakap, where desilting work, coupled with stronger monitoring and enforcement, had helped improve the river’s condition.
“We are now working to clean up and rehabilitate the area to improve the environment for residents, especially those living near Kampung Selamat,” he said.
H’ng said the authorities would not hesitate to take action against farmers who breached the regulations, including by releasing sewage waste directly into drains or rivers, stressing that offenders would be issued with summonses and their cases referred to the courts. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to discuss further action on Sarawak haze with Abang Jo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR,  Sept  4 — Further action, including the possibility of declaring a disaster emergency following an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeding 500 in Serian, will be discussed with the Sarawak government, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said he had contacted Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday to discuss the matter.
He also assured that appropriate safety measures, including the suspension of office and school operations, except for critical agencies, would be implemented should an emergency be declared due to worsening API readings.
“We will take all necessary measures, whether cloud seeding or other actions, even though this (haze situation) is the result of developments elsewhere.
“We have to bear the consequences and be patient for a while. I pray for the safety of the people in Serian, across Sarawak and in other affected areas,” he told a press conference after performing Friday prayers at the Bukit Indah Mosque in Ampang Jaya.
This morning, air quality in Serian, Sarawak, remained at a hazardous level, with the monitoring station at the local District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website, Kuching also recorded a reading in the hazardous range at 310. Two other areas in Sarawak were at the “very unhealthy” level: Samarahan with a reading of 281 and Sri Aman (245). — Bernama

Title: Azalina calls for red flags at Desaru beaches after three teens drown
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — Pengerang Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas.
She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities (PBT), particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming.
“This is important, especially during the school holidays when more visitors are expected to visit the beaches,” she told a press conference after visiting the family of a drowning victim at Pantai Tanjung Lompat here today.
Azalina, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), advised families to avoid sea activities from September to December due to strong winds.
She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.
On the need for beach patrol or lifeguards, Azalina said the matter should be studied as the coastline in Pengerang is extensive and would involve additional costs, unlike resorts where lifeguards are part of the management.
She said sea conditions in Pengerang differ from those in several other coastal areas such as Terengganu, Mersing and Tioman, as the area is a trade route with strong currents.
According to her, strong winds can also cause the sea to appear calm on the surface even when it is unsafe, as there may be strong or swirling currents beneath the water.
Three of the four victims in Wednesday morning’s incident have so far been found drowned. They were Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor and Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, all aged 16.
The search for the fourth victim, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian, who remains missing, is ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Lorry driver remanded three days over crash that killed 12-year-old boy in Gurun
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police have detained a 40-year-old lorry driver over a crash involving a motorcycle on Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday that killed a 12-year-old boy.
The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, 12, died at the scene from severe injuries.
Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspect was detained to assist investigations into the crash,
Harian Metro
reported.
“The suspect was remanded for three days from today to assist investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said when contacted today.
In the crash yesterday, the victim is believed to have been riding a motorcycle when it collided with the rear left side of a lorry at the scene.
The victim’s 14-year-old friend, who was riding pillion, escaped with minor scratches and cuts to his hands and legs.
The deceased was a Year Six pupil at a school in Paya Mak Insun, Pendang, and lived in Kampung Paya Mak Insun, Ayer Puteh, Pendang.
The pillion rider is from Kampung Batu 3, Jalan Jeniang, and is a Form Two student at a secondary school in Batu 5, Gurun.

Title: Retired military officer with ‘Datuk’ title charged over alleged caddie molestation in Ayer Keroh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — A 68-year-old retired military officer holding the title “Datuk” was charged in the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court here today with using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 20-year-old female caddie last month.
According to
Harian Metro
, Yahya Hashim pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him before Magistrate Uthman Abd Ghani.
The charge alleged that Yahya used criminal force against the victim with intent to outrage her modesty at the Tiara Melaka Golf & Country Club golf course in Jalan Gapam, Bukit Katil, in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, between 8.30am and 12.30pm on August 25.
The offence falls under Section 354 of the Penal Code, which provides for up to 10 years’ imprisonment, or a fine, or whipping, or any two of the punishments upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Syauqi Mardia Baharudin offered bail of RM5,000 with an additional condition that the accused not disturb the victim, as the location of the alleged offence is her workplace.
Lawyer Melvin Tay, representing Yahya, asked the court to reduce the bail amount, saying his client was retired, had no fixed income and lived with his wife.
The court was also told that Yahya had a prostate-related health condition requiring treatment.
Magistrate Uthman then allowed Yahya to be released on RM2,500 bail with one surety, while agreeing to the prosecution’s additional condition that he not disturb the victim until the case is concluded.
The court fixed September 28 for mention of the case.

Title: Perlis police arrest activist over incendiary TikTok on Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 4 — A 55-year-old activist has been remanded for two days from today on suspicion of making an inciting post via social media related to the organisation of a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple here on Aug 22.
Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the man, who works as a consultant, was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor yesterday at 10 am.
He said that earlier, the Perlis police received 14 reports regarding posts on the activist’s TikTok application between Aug 22 and 27.
“The post contained a picture of the organisation of the ‘Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali’ which was held on Aug 30, 2026, from 9 am to 11 am at the Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil site in Bukit Lagi, Kangar,” he said in a statement today.
Yusharifuddin said the investigation found that the organisation of the gathering was believed to be a response to dissatisfaction with the temple that was demolished by the authorities on Aug 20, in accordance with the law.
He said the activist is suspected of wanting to incite the Indian Hindu community to support actions contrary to existing laws and statutes, and the case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“This gathering is also considered a very dangerous incitement that could trigger religious and racial riots in the state of Perlis,” he also said. — Bernama

Title: Third missing teenager’s body recovered at Kota Tinggi beach
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — The body of a third missing teenager has been recovered from the waters near Tanjung Siang, following a tragic incident at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar.
The victim, 16-year-old Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, was found floating by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 11.15am today, approximately five kilometres from the site of the initial incident.
Kota Tinggi deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed the discovery.
“The body has been taken to the Crime Scene Control (CSC) centre at 11.45am for identification by the next of kin before further action,”  he said when contacted today.
Mohd Najib Sam, the acting director of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) Tanjung Sedili Zone, confirmed that the victim was positively identified as Muhammad Adib. The body has since been moved to the Kota Tinggi Hospital forensics unit for a post-mortem examination.
“The SAR team will continue the operation for the fourth and last victim,” Najib said in a statement today.
The search area has been expanded and refined to 103 square nautical miles, with operations coordinated by the Johor Bahru Maritime Rescue Sub Centre (MRSC).
Rescue teams are currently contending with challenging conditions, including south-southwest winds of 20 to 30 kilometres per hour and wave heights between 1.0 and 1.5 metres.
Today’s operation involved 61 personnel from various agencies, supported by volunteers from the local community.
Of the four teenagers originally reported missing, three have now been recovered, including Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul and Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, both aged 16.
The SAR operation, now in its third day, remains focused on locating the final missing teenager, Muhammad Haiman Fitri Supian.

Title: MAG says mass drug screenings for Malaysia Airlines crew near 100pc
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed drug screenings for nearly all Malaysia Airlines cabin crew following the arrest of a pilot in Jakarta, president and group chief executive officer Capt. Nasaruddin A. Bakar said today.
Nasaruddin told reporters that 98.8 per cent of the carrier’s 2,840 cabin crew members have tested negative so far, with the remaining 1.2 per cent scheduled to undergo screening today.
“It will be an ongoing process, including for pilots,” Nasaruddin said following an event announcing new route launches for Malaysia Airlines and its budget subsidiary Firefly.
MAG, the parent company of the flag carrier, ordered mass drug testing across its cabin operations last month after an off-duty Malaysia Airlines second officer was detained in Indonesia on July 29.
Indonesian authorities arrested the pilot at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after discovering 25 kilograms of ecstasy pills and 2.7 grams of methamphetamine in his luggage.
The pilot, who was traveling in the cockpit jump seat as a passenger, tested positive for methamphetamine, ecstasy, and cocaine.
He was allegedly promised RM50,000 to transport the illicit drugs.
On Aug 17, MAG announced that all operationally active Malaysia Airlines pilots had undergone drug tests and tested negative. Nasaruddin suggested the company plans to make testing continuous.
“We will do random tests and it would be frequent,” he told reporters.

Title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Busan flights starting December
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Airlines will resume flights to Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, starting December this year as the national carrier expands its network and pushes to return to profitability.
Malaysian Aviation Group chief executive officer Capt Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the Busan service is one of several new routes the airline group expects to launch, including expansion by its budget unit Firefly, which recently added China's Kunming to its destination network.

Title: Two dead in Jasin motorcycle crash after overtaking manoeuvre fails
Article:
JASIN, Sept 4 — Two motorcyclists were killed in an accident on Jalan Gapam near a petrol station in Bemban here last night.
Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said both victims, a 21-year-old college student and a 41-year-old lorry driver, died on the spot in the incident, which occurred at about 11.30 pm.
He said initial investigations found that the student was travelling from Bemban towards Ayer Keroh, while the lorry driver was heading in the opposite direction, towards Bemban from Ayer Keroh.
“The 41-year-old motorcyclist was believed to have entered the opposite lane while overtaking a vehicle before colliding with the motorcycle ridden by the 21-year-old victim, who was travelling straight in his lane.
“Both victims sustained serious head and body injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
Lee said police were unable to obtain any CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident.
He said both motorcycles sustained front-end damage and were sent to the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) in Alor Gajah for inspection.
“The post-mortem will be conducted today at the Jasin Hospital Forensic Unit after the body identification process is completed,” he said, adding that the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: PAS sets seven priorities for GE16, including wider political cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — PAS has outlined seven strategic priorities as it prepares for the 16th General Election (GE16), including remaining open to cooperation with any political party as long as its principles are upheld.
The
New Straits Times
reported that PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party’s Muslim unity agenda would see it continue defending Islam while honouring agreements reached with other parties.
“PAS is prepared to cooperate with any party on matters that benefit the country without compromising its policies and principles,” he said.
“These unity efforts are not limited to the national level but are also being embraced at the state, constituency and branch levels,” he said.
Abdul Hadi was speaking when delivering his policy speech at the opening of PAS’ 72nd Annual Muktamar in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, today.
He said the second priority was to defend PAS’ victories in the SG4 states of Kelantan, Kedah, Terengganu and Perlis, with the party seeking to retain every state and parliamentary seat it won in GE15.
The third priority is to expand PAS’ electoral gains in targeted states, while the fourth focuses on strengthening support among ulama, youth and Muslimat voters, as well as members of the Dewan Himpunan Pendukung PAS (DHPP).
The fifth priority is strengthening tarbiah and the party’s organisational structure, while the sixth centres on election machinery and information efforts aimed at securing victory.
Abdul Hadi said this would include selecting candidates who meet the required criteria, particularly those who demonstrate commitment to the party, integrity and influence within their communities.
The seventh priority is high-impact dakwah and welfare programmes.
Abdul Hadi also urged PAS members and its election machinery to use the muktamar for self-reflection while taking guidance from this year’s theme, “Islamic Solutions for Victory”.
He called on party members to strengthen their unity and discipline while widening PAS’ influence through dakwah, welfare and efforts to unite Muslims.

Title: Tahfiz students perform prayers to support search for missing teens in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — For the second consecutive day, students of Madrasah Tahfiz Al-Quran Ar-Redha in Bandar Penawar recited the azan and Yasin and performed Dhuha and hajat prayers as the search continued for two teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach here.
Islamic Education teacher Mohd Azroy Azhar said the students took the initiative voluntarily after seeing the various efforts by the authorities and the victims’ families to locate the missing teenagers.
He said the students were also doing their part by offering prayers and supplications, hoping that the two missing teenagers would be found soon.
“We feel that this is one way for these tahfiz children to serve the community. We want to show that whatever test we go through, there is a solution. Allah SWT tells us in the Quran to face our trials with patience and prayer.
“We pray to Allah SWT that they can be found today. The family is really hoping for good news. Insya-Allah, we turn to the Quran and prayers for strength,” he said when met at Tanjung Lompat Beach here today.
Four 16-year-old boys were initially reported missing after they were feared to have drowned while swimming at the beach on Wednesday.
The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 8.19 am regarding the incident involving six teenagers from a group of 15 who had been camping in the area for three days.
Two of them, Mohamad Faqrul Isqandar Abdullah and Muhammad Afiq Ruzaini Mazlan, both 16, were rescued by members of the public at about 7.45 am, while four others were reported missing.
Two of the four teenagers initially reported missing have since been found drowned, namely Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor and Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, while Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal and Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian remain missing. — Bernama

Title: Police refer case of man accused of provoking crowd at National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to DPP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) after referring an investigation paper on a man accused of causing a disturbance and provoking the crowd during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31.
Putrajaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the investigation paper was referred to the DPP’s office yesterday for further action, BuletinTV3 reported.
“The investigation paper is still with the DPP’s office and we are awaiting further instructions from the authorities concerned.
“So far, we have recorded statements from seven witnesses to assist investigations into the cause of the provocation, which was reportedly linked to a dispute over seats on the day,” he said when contacted today.
Police had previously reported that a man was detained for allegedly causing a disturbance and provoking members of the public during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.
Further investigations found that the man tested positive for THC, a compound associated with cannabis.
Aidi Sham was quoted as saying the 30-year-old suspect turned himself in at the Putrajaya district police headquarters at 12.15am on Wednesday.
Police had earlier recorded statements from seven people in connection with the case, while the 30-year-old cook was detained in Putrajaya after five police reports were lodged against him.
A video that went viral on social media showed a man wearing an orange-brown shirt allegedly provoking people and barging into and pushing members of the public waiting for the seating area gates to open, triggering a scuffle in which several people fell.

Title: Serian API hits hazardous 518, emergency declaration possible
Article:
SERIAN, Sept 4 — Serian recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518 as of 10 am today, placing it in the “hazardous” category amid transboundary haze.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), an API reading above 300 is classified as hazardous, while readings between 201 and 300 are categorised as “very unhealthy”.
Kuching also recorded a hazardous API reading of 310, followed by Kota Samarahan at 281 and Sri Aman at 245.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas had previously said areas recording API readings of 500 could be declared under a state of emergency by the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).
However, he said such a declaration would apply only to the affected localities and not the entire state.
Cloud seeding operations have also been conducted at several locations in Sarawak to increase water storage levels and help mitigate the impact of the haze. — Bernama

Title: Six held over Malaysian co-pilot’s Jakarta drug case after four fled to Thailand, Vietnam and returned
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN) has detained six local men over a drug smuggling case involving a Malaysian co-pilot arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, Indonesia, with four of the suspects having fled to Thailand and Vietnam after learning of his arrest.
The six were detained in a special operation conducted between August 20 and 28, following information obtained from questioning of the 39-year-old co-pilot by a team of JSJN officers sent to Jakarta from August 11 to 15,
Berita Haria
n reported.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the six were believed to have acted as suppliers and couriers who provided drugs to the co-pilot.
“All of them, aged between 23 and 50, were detained in a special operation conducted by JSJN between August 20 and 28,” he said when contacted today.
“Based on investigations and intelligence, they played the roles of ‘upline’ and ‘downline’ in the drug distribution syndicate involving the co-pilot,” he added.
Meanwhile,
Harian Metro
reported that Hussein said two of the suspects had fled to Thailand while another two went to Vietnam after learning of the co-pilot’s arrest.
The two who fled to Thailand were arrested when they returned to Malaysia by ferry through Kuah, Langkawi, Kedah, while the other two were detained after arriving at Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas.
The remaining two suspects were arrested in Bukit Mertajam, Penang and Klang, Selangor.
Hussein said investigations were ongoing and all six were being detained under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
Under the Act, police can detain suspects for up to 60 days to complete investigations before a further detention order is issued.
He said JSJN would also share information obtained from the investigation with the Indonesian National Police (Polri).
The co-pilot was arrested at the International Arrivals Terminal of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur on Malaysia Airlines flight MH727.
The arrest was made at about 11.30pm local time after Indonesian customs officers detected suspicious luggage during an X-ray scan and directed him to an inspection room after he collected the bag.
A search found 14 packets containing 70,114 ecstasy pills weighing about 25kg in the luggage, as well as four grammes of methamphetamine in his hand luggage, with the drugs estimated to be worth RM45 million.
Indonesian police said the co-pilot had allegedly been promised RM50,000 to transport the drugs to Jakarta before they were to be collected by another person from a hotel.

Title: Appeals court grants Najib and son stay of bankruptcy action in RM1.7b tax case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The Court of Appeal here today granted former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak and his son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin, a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against them.
A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Ong Chee Kwan allowed their appeals to set aside the High Court’s decision on Nov 17 last year, which had dismissed their applications for a stay.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Alwi said the stay was warranted as the appellants had raised specific issues to be determined before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT), which constituted sufficient grounds for granting the applications.
Najib and Nazifuddin had sought a stay of the bankruptcy proceedings pending the disposal of their appeals before the SCIT against additional tax assessments issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
The bankruptcy proceedings stemmed from separate High Court decisions granting the IRB summary judgments against the father and son over unpaid tax arrears for the 2011 to 2017 assessment years.
The IRB is seeking to recover RM1.69 billion from Najib and RM37.6 million from Nazifuddin. — Bernama

Title: Three girls caught fighting in viral social media video in Kuala Pilah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police are investigating a fight involving three teenage girls that went viral on social media after the incident at Dataran Melang in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan.
According to Kosmo! Online, Kuala Pilah district police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said the incident involved a 15-year-old schoolgirl who went to the location with her brother to meet two acquaintances over a misunderstanding linked to the circulation of her photograph on social media.
“During the meeting, a scuffle broke out between the complainant and the two individuals, causing the teenager to suffer injuries before she returned home with her family,” he said when contacted.
Muhamad Mustafah said the girl and her father later went to the home of one of the individuals yesterday to discuss the matter before lodging a police report.
“Police view the incident seriously and investigations are under way to identify the actual cause of the fight and those involved,” he said.
A video of the incident had earlier gone viral on social media, showing the girls pulling at each other and kicking during the fight.

Title: EC reaffirms commitment to fairness and transparency on 69th anniversary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Election Commission (EC), which marks its 69th anniversary today, has reaffirmed its commitment to managing the country’s electoral process fairly, transparently, efficiently and with integrity.
In a Facebook post today, the EC said that over its 69-year history, it had continued to evolve with the times in strengthening the country’s democratic system through elections.
The EC has also continued to improve its service delivery to the public, with greater efficiency and transparency.
“May the EC continue to move forward with integrity and remain a trusted democratic institution in safeguarding and strengthening the country’s democratic process.
“The EC, efficient and transparent,” according to the post.
The EC was established on Sept 4, 1957, in accordance with Article 114 of the Federal Constitution, with its membership initially comprising a chairman and two members.
Datuk Dr Mustafa Albakri Hassan served as the commission’s first chairman, with Lee Ewe Boon and Ditt Singh as its two members.
Following the formation of Malaysia in 1963, the commission’s membership was increased to three, with the additional member appointed from either Sabah or Sarawak on a rotating basis.
The EC was expanded to seven members in 2002, comprising a chairman, deputy chairman and five members, including one representative each from Sabah and Sarawak. — Bernama

Title: PAS does not need manifesto pledge on gambling ban, says Kedah MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — PAS does not need to include its opposition to gambling in its election manifesto because the stance is already part of the party’s core principles, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor.
Sanusi, who is also PAS central election director, said the public could refer to Clause 5 of the PAS Constitution, which clearly states that the party seeks to uphold Islamic values and laws in governance, including Syariah laws prohibiting gambling premises and regulating the sale of alcohol,
Berita Harian
reported.
He said people should rely on effort, prayer and trust in God to achieve success in life rather than turn to gambling.
“I hope the people in this state and society as a whole will stay away from gambling and not make luck a means of getting through life,” he said.
“PAS’ position on the prohibition of gambling is clear and based on Islamic principles, and does not depend on whether the matter is included in an election manifesto or not,” he added.
He was speaking to reporters after the Anak Muda Podcast held in conjunction with the 72nd PAS Muktamar at the Pusat Tarbiah Islamiah Kelantan in Pengkalan Chepa here last night.
Sanusi was responding to a video by Perlis Mufti Datuk Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin challenging PAS to include gambling and alcohol in its election manifesto.
The video was circulated by a portal’s Facebook account.
Sanusi said there was no need to include such matters in a manifesto as the document was essentially a political party’s offer to voters, rather than a restatement of policies or principles already enshrined in its constitution.
“People say a manifesto is not a holy book. Read the PAS Constitution. What is PAS fighting for? But if people do not want PAS, they will still refuse to accept it, right? They will find all sorts of reasons.
“Islam prohibits gambling! Do we really have to put that in the manifesto too? Why not include the declaration of faith as well?” he said.
On the gambling premises issue, Sanusi said the state government was still awaiting further developments, including possible legal proceedings should gambling operators seek compensation through the courts.
“We will wait for the next steps. They also want to take the matter to court to seek compensation. We will fight it,” he said.

Title: Man injured in suspected shooting at Machang Bubok used car workshop
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 4 — A 43-year-old local man was injured after he was believed to have been shot at a used-car workshop near a Chinese cemetery along Jalan Sungai Lembu in Machang Bubok yesterday.
Seberang Perai Tengah district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police received a report on the incident at about 2.05pm.
“Initial investigations found that at about 1.05pm, the victim was approached by two men of unknown race on a motorcycle.
“One of the suspects is believed to have fired a shot towards the victim,” he said in a statement today.
The victim fled to the Chinese cemetery to save himself, while both suspects fled from the scene.
He sustained an injury and a fracture to his right palm.
“He is being treated in the hospital and is in stable condition,” Nik Aminuddin said.
Police found several items believed to be connected to the incident at the scene.
Nik Aminuddin said police are investigating to identify the suspects and establish the motive.
“The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code,” he said
He called on those with information related to the case to contact their nearest police station or investigating officer ASP Muazzam Shaaban at 017-4825017.
He also advised the public not to speculate or spread unverified information about the incident.

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls for action against Zahid over RM2.1b Rural Development Ministry overspending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — DAP’s Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has called for Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and the Rural and Regional Development Ministry to face action after the ministry spent RM2.1 billion more than its approved allocations over three years.
Lim said allowing spending beyond approved allocations could set a bad precedent, with other ministries potentially repeating the practice in ways that could affect the national treasury and financial stability.
He described Zahid’s actions as irresponsible, saying they breached existing financial procedures and could lead to enforcement under relevant laws.
“What Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has done directly threatens financial security and economic stability,” he said in a statement today.
Lim said the potential consequences should be considered if all ministries were allowed to spend freely without taking into account whether the country could afford such expenditure.
He also questioned which contractors benefited from Rural and Regional Development Ministry projects that resulted in spending exceeding approved allocations, and whether they had been selected according to regulations through a transparent, open and accountable process.
Lim cited Finance Ministry figures showing the ministry spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion.
In 2024, spending rose to RM2 billion against RM1.3 billion allocated, while RM2.3 billion was spent in 2025 against an allocation of RM1.6 billion.
He said the total excess spending amounted to RM2.1 billion from 2023 to 2025, when the ministry was under Zahid’s leadership.
Lim said RM2.1 billion was a significant amount, adding that similar overspending had not been an issue in the years before 2023.
He also pointed to the government’s restrictions on support letters issued by ministries other than the Finance Ministry, saying such letters could amount to hidden government guarantees.
Lim said only the Finance Ministry was permitted to issue support letters or guarantees under the country’s financial laws, citing previous action over a support letter issued by the Transport Ministry without its approval.
As deputy prime minister, Lim said Zahid should set an example of prudent spending and explain fully to Malaysians why the ministry had exceeded its approved allocations.

Title: ‘Snow’ on Kesas? It was actually soap foam after heavy rain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — What looked like snow covering part of the Shah Alam Expressway (Kesas) yesterday afternoon turned out to be soap foam triggered by heavy rain washing up residue from a spill more than a week ago.
The unusual scene stretched about 500 metres between Kilometre 30 and 30.5 of the Klang-bound-to-Kuala Lumpur side of Kesas and was spotted at about 3.10pm.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said initial investigations found the soap residue likely came from a lorry load that spilled on August 24 near the Kota Kemuning slip road before the vehicle entered Kesas heading towards Klang, Kosmo! Online reported.
“When the spill happened, firefighters took action by spreading sawdust along the affected stretch to clean up the soap residue,” he said in a statement last night.
“However, heavy rain today caused the remaining soap residue to produce foam along about 500 metres of the highway,” he added.
Sarudin said the highway concessionaire subsequently carried out a second round of cleaning, which was completed at 4.58pm today.
The white-covered stretch attracted attention on social media, with motorists sharing videos showing what appeared to be a snow-covered roadway.
The videos showed a white liquid coating the road surface, with tyre tracks visible from vehicles that had passed through the affected area.
The incident also raised concerns among road users, particularly motorcyclists, over reports that the road had become slippery.

Title: Johari Abdul: Parliament must tackle Malaysia’s ageing, smaller families through effective legislation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Parliament must translate demographic challenges such as ageing populations, smaller families and changing intergenerational needs into concrete laws, budgets and policies, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.
He said population and development issues were ultimately political questions as public priorities must find expression through legislation, institutions and government spending.
“Words create attention. Attention creates pressure. Pressure creates priorities and priorities eventually appear in legislation, institutions and budgets,” he said at a welcome dinner he hosted for participants of the Asian Forum of Parliamentarians on Population and Development (AFPPD) Annual Conference 2026 here yesterday.
Also present were Works Minister and President of AFPPD Malaysia Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi and his deputy, who is also Ipoh Timur Member of Parliament Howard Lee Chuan How.
Johari said he was pleased that ageing, an issue often associated with criticism or speculation in political circles, was instead being given a firm place on the policy agenda at the conference.
“Parliamentarians have a complicated relationship with age. When we are young, people tell us we lack experience. When we acquire experience, people begin asking when we intend to retire.
“So I am delighted to attend a conference where, for once, ageing is neither criticism nor speculation. It is an important item on the agenda,” he said.
Johari said the issues discussed by parliamentarians at the conference went beyond population statistics, encompassing how societies prepare young people for adulthood, support families, value care and enable women to participate fully in society.
He said they also included the challenge of responding to longer life expectancy at a time when families were becoming smaller.
According to Johari, the work of AFPPD was particularly important as demographic changes unfolded over decades, while electoral politics often operated within much shorter timeframes.
Recalling Malaysia’s journey towards hosting the AFPPD Global Secretariat, he said the initiative began after AFPPD Malaysia returned from Tokyo in April 2024, when then deputy president Lee approached him with the proposal.
He said Lee had explained why Malaysia was well positioned to host the secretariat and why Parliament should provide the necessary political and institutional support.
Johari said he subsequently participated in AFPPD Malaysia’s regional meeting in Kuala Lumpur in July 2024, which focused on ageing preparedness and the care economy.
“Two years later, the Global Secretariat is here. So Howard (Lee), congratulations. You kept pursuing it through Parliament, government and AFPPD, and you have delivered what you said Malaysia should set out to achieve,” he added.
Johari congratulated AFPPD, its member states, Nanta and the entire team on establishing the Global Secretariat in Malaysia, stressing that its success should not be measured by the number of conferences or communiques issued, but by whether parliamentary cooperation translates into laws, budgets, oversight and action.
He said the inauguration of the AFPPD Global Secretariat office in Kuala Lumpur tomorrow would mark a new chapter in parliamentary cooperation on population and development.
The two-day conference, themed “Parliamentary Leadership for the Future: An All of Society Approach to the Care Economy and Demographic Resilience”, brings together parliamentarians from Asia, the Pacific, Africa and the Arab world. — Bernama
